newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: New meeting on Western Sahara in London on weekend.
newsitem.headline: New meeting on Western Sahara in London on weekend.

text.p: Former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker will resume direct talks with parties to the dispute in the Western Sahara in London this weekend, the United Nations said on Tuesday.
U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said the talks would take place on Saturday and Sunday and would continue in the future "for so long as they hold any promise of progress in Mr Baker's opinion."

The United Nations has been trying for years to organise a referendum to decide whether Western Sahara should be incorporated into Morocco, which controls most of the former Spanish colony, or become independent, as sought by the Algerian-backed Polisario Front.
The ballot, originally set for January 1992, has been repeatedly postponed because of a disagreement between the two sides over who should be eligible to vote.
Baker, the U.N. special envoy for the Western Sahara, met both parties in Lisbon last month and presented new proposals in an attempt to break the deadlock over the territory's future.

The Lisbon talks were the first formal talks between opponents who fought a 16-year war over the territory. Morocco and the Polisario Front were believed to have held secret meetings last August and September in Geneva and Tangier in their first direct encounter since 1993.
In Lisbon, Baker said his proposals were partly based on existing plans but contained new elements.

He has been asked by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan to recommend whether the U.N. peace plan calling for a referendum can be carried out, or whether agreed adjustments could be made or other means found to resolve the dispute.
Eckhard said Algeria and Mauritania would attend the London talks as observers.
